edges.notes: RHEL ships supported Linux kernel streams for enterprise architectures as part of the distribution.
RHEL on standard ports uses glibc as the C library alongside the dynamic linker.
systemd is the default init and service manager on supported RHEL major releases per Red Hat documentation.
RHEL services are expressed as systemd unit files and drop-ins on default systemd installs.
RHEL userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
GCC toolchain packages participate in RHEL developer toolsets and RPM build flows.
GNU binutils participate in standard RHEL RPM build and link flows.
g++-built packages link GNU libstdc++ above glibc on typical RHEL GNU/Linux flows.
LLVM/Clang toolchains may be installed from RHEL or related repositories where offered.
Official and certified RHEL-base OCI images and Podman/Docker-style workflows are common in field patterns; Docker pulls RHEL-class bases where published.
CRI/containerd nodes run RHEL-derived workload images pulled as OCI artifacts in Kubernetes-class deployments.
RHEL is a common node OS for on-prem and vendor Kubernetes platforms including OpenShift-class footprints.
RHEL userlands are packaged as OCI image rootfs layers where vendors publish UBI or RHEL bases.
Red Hat documents OpenShift Container Platform as running on RHEL-class nodes in typical product deployments.
Substitutable Linux distribution defaults for containers and servers (glibc/systemd enterprise vs musl/OpenRC field patterns).
Rocky Linux rebuilds and tracks RHEL-compatible major/minor streams with independent community governance.
AlmaLinux rebuilds and tracks RHEL-compatible major/minor streams with independent foundation governance.
Historical CentOS Linux releases aligned RHEL-compatible major/minor streams prior to the CentOS Stream pivot and documented EOL timelines.
